headline: MARKETS IN LIMBO: Gold Holds $4,362, Silver at $64.39 as Metals Enter Pre-FOMC Standstill 3 Days Out
snippet: Gold spot held at $4,362.28 per ounce and silver steadied at $64.39 on Saturday September 12 as both metals enter near-complete paralysis ahead of the Federal Reserve's September 15-16 rate decision. A modest Friday recovery — gold +0.77%, silver +1.46% — failed to reverse the three-consecutive-weekly-loss trend, with 30-year Treasury yields above 7% and rate-hike odds at ~90% keeping the dollar bid and metals sellers active. The binary setup is now widely understood: a hawkish hike could flush the crowded 228,000-contract managed-money net long position toward the $4,050–$4,100 support zone, while a hold or dovish pivot would ignite a short-covering rally above $4,720 resistance. Saturday's muted session reflects a market that has made its pre-FOMC positioning decisions and is now simply waiting. For retail investors, the key observation is that gold is holding above $4,300 despite historic rate-hike pressure — a structural signal that the underlying bull thesis remains intact regardless of Tuesday's outcome.

headline: LME RECORD SMASHED THEN ERASED: Copper Hit All-Time High $14,875, Lost $563 in One Session on Tariff U-Turn
snippet: The week produced the most dramatic copper price swing in LME history. Copper surged to an all-time LME record of $14,875 per tonne on September 7 as tariff speculation and Chile-Peru supply concerns drove a scramble for physical stockpiles — then crashed $563 (3.1%) to $14,312 per tonne in a single session on September 11, the largest intraday LME copper reversal on record, after Reuters reported the White House had not finalised its refined copper tariff position. US COMEX copper futures mirrored the move, plunging from a session record high to $6.45/lb. The near-$600/tonne round trip in one LME session reflects how crowded tariff-speculation positioning had become. For junior copper developers, the week simultaneously validates the long-term demand thesis — copper demand is strong enough to produce all-time record prices — while illustrating the political binary that overshadows near-term economics: tariff premium economics can dissolve in a Reuters headline.

headline: NEW ZEALAND'S BEST EVER HIT: Rua Gold Drills 136 g/t AuEq at Auld Creek — Antimony Accounts for 40% of Value
snippet: Rua Gold Inc. (TSX: RUA) reported its highest-grade drill results to date at the Auld Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Reefton, New Zealand on September 8 — standout hole ACDDH119 cut 0.6 metres at 136.2 g/t gold equivalent (82.9 g/t gold + 24.80% antimony). At current antimony prices near $60,000/tonne, the antimony component alone represents roughly 40% of gross metal value in that interval, making Auld Creek one of the highest-value gold-antimony systems in active drilling outside China. The completed 19,600-metre program also returned 2.7 metres at 23.2 g/t AuEq, 7.0 metres at 9.9 g/t AuEq, and 32.0 metres at 2.4 g/t AuEq — confirming breadth alongside the headline peak. The project was accepted under New Zealand's Fast-Track Approvals regime in July 2026, with the formal Mining Application scheduled for October and a Pre-Feasibility Study targeted for December 2026. Four rigs will continue drilling through Q4 to test strike and depth extensions. For junior mining investors, Rua Gold combines a near-term development timeline with exposure to one of the world's most supply-constrained critical defence materials.

headline: HILLGROVE TRIPLE PLAY: Larvotto Drills 62.6 g/t AuEq PLUS 7.27% Tungsten PLUS Antimony in a Single NSW Mine
snippet: Larvotto Resources (ASX: LRV) reported high-grade gold, antimony and tungsten results on September 7 from new drilling at the Clarks Gully target within its Hillgrove operation in New South Wales — just as the mine entered production. Standout hole CLG128 cut 9.5 metres at 8.07 g/t gold equivalent from 345.5 metres, including 0.5 metres at 62.6 g/t AuEq, and returned 6.1 metres at 1.43% tungsten trioxide (WO3). Hole CLG136 delivered 9 metres at 7.05 g/t AuEq including a 7.27% WO3 peak. The current Clarks Gully resource stands at 647,000 tonnes at 1.6% antimony and 2.1 g/t gold, with engineering and metallurgical studies advancing toward a Mineral Reserve and underground mining application. Larvotto is uniquely positioned as the only publicly listed company with operating and expanding production in three simultaneously critical Western-supply-constrained commodities — gold at record prices, antimony subject to Chinese export restrictions, and tungsten predominantly sourced from China — all at a single Australian tier-1 site.

headline: ALASKA VMS STRIKE: Silver47 Hits 74m of Massive Sulfide at Brand-New 'Second Chance Zone' at Red Mountain
snippet: Silver47 Exploration Corp. (TSXV: AGA) completed its 2026 summer drill program at the Red Mountain Project in Alaska on September 8, announcing a new discovery in the process: the Second Chance Zone, where 74 metres of visually observed semi-massive to massive sulfide intervals were intercepted within a broader 197-metre zone of continuous sulfide mineralization. A second 50-metre sulfide intercept was identified at the nearby Dry Creek target. The 4,136-metre, 14-hole program tested priority volcanogenic massive sulfide (VMS) targets across the high-grade silver-zinc-gold-copper Red Mountain system, located 100 kilometres south of Fairbanks. Assay results are pending — visual observation of thick massive sulfide horizons is the most reliable precursor to high-grade economic mineralization in VMS systems. At current silver prices above $64/oz, confirmation of economic VMS grades at Second Chance would represent a significant resource growth event for a company already holding a defined high-grade silver equivalent resource in a proven Alaskan gold-silver belt.

headline: SERBIAN SKARN MONSTER: DPM Metals Hits 246m at 1.36% CuEq, Ramps to 15 Rigs at Čoka Rakita Copper-Gold Belt
snippet: DPM Metals Inc. (TSX: DPM, ASX: DPM) reported September 8 assay results from its Dumitru Potok copper-gold-silver skarn project on the Čoka Rakita licence in Serbia: drillhole BIDD253 returned 246 metres at 1.36% copper equivalent (0.67% Cu, 0.69 g/t Au, 4.21 g/t Ag), extending marble-hosted skarn mineralization 90 metres west. The bonanza-grade core delivered in DPDD042 — 50 metres at 3.68% CuEq (2.18% Cu, 1.36 g/t Au, 21.75 g/t Ag) — confirms a high-grade skarn envelope within the broader system. At Rakita North, hole RADDGTH009C intersected 76 metres at 2.66% CuEq. DPM Metals is expanding its 2026 program to 32,000–35,000 metres with plans to run 15 rigs on the Čoka Rakita licence by year-end. The existing Rakita Camp inferred resource stands at 2.6 million ounces gold and 1.9 billion pounds copper. Against the backdrop of copper's all-time LME record this week and sustained demand from energy transition infrastructure, large-scale European copper-gold skarn systems in politically stable jurisdictions are attracting significant institutional attention.

headline: THE BULL HOLDS: Money Metals Shows Why September's Fed-Driven Selloff Is a Buying Window, Not a Structural Break
snippet: Writing September 9 in the wake of a stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report, Money Metals Exchange makes the counter-consensus case: the September selloff in gold and silver is a tactical correction inside a secular bull market, not evidence of structural breakdown. The article notes that every significant gold decline in 2026 has created a buying window for investors with position discipline, while those who sold into Fed-fear rallies repeatedly re-entered at higher prices. With gold near $4,380 after recently challenging $4,500 and silver testing the $64 support zone, Money Metals frames the September correction as consistent with the pattern of a maturing bull that periodically clears crowded longs before reasserting the primary trend. The structural case remains intact: central banks bought 289 tonnes in Q2 alone — a quarterly record — dollar reserve share continues to erode, and sovereign debt dynamics provide a durable bid beneath spot prices that operates independently of near-term FOMC outcomes. A useful perspective for retail investors tempted to exit ahead of Tuesday's binary event.

headline: ANGLO TECK CLOCK STARTS: September Window Opens for Mining's Biggest Deal — China and South Korea Hold the Keys
snippet: The Anglo American-Teck Resources merger entered its allowed closing window in September 2026, as the only outstanding regulatory approvals from China and South Korea are now due. Shareholder votes passed in December 2025, Investment Canada cleared simultaneously, and the future Anglo Teck Executive Leadership Team was announced July 30 — with Anglo American CEO Duncan Wanblad leading the combined entity and Teck's Jonathan Price as Deputy CEO. The deal creates Anglo Teck plc, a top-5 global copper producer headquartered in Vancouver, targeting US$800 million in annual pre-tax synergies within four years of close. For junior copper developers globally, the combination signals sustained major-house appetite for large-scale copper exposure and removes two historically active acquirers from the deal pool — potentially redirecting acquisition activity toward tier-2 operators, royalty companies, and quality TSX-V copper developers with resources that could fill Anglo Teck's organic pipeline gap. The September–March window means deal closure is increasingly likely before year-end.

headline: AUSTRALIA RESTARTS BITE: Lithium Slips to 3-Week Low Sept 12 as Mine Supply Offsets China Demand Uncertainty
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices fell to approximately CNY 142,250–143,000 per tonne as of September 11-12, 2026 — the lowest in nearly one month — as Australia's mine restart wave continues to add supply just as China's Jianxiawo mine (CATL, ~4% of global supply) remains idled. Mineral Resources' Bald Hill mine resumed production in July at nameplate capacity of 165,000 dry metric tonnes per year and Core Lithium's Finniss operation produced its first spodumene concentrate this week, collectively adding meaningful Australian output to the global balance. The paradox: Chinese domestic supply is tighter-than-normal due to ongoing environmental enforcement at Jianxiawo, but total global supply expectations are rising as Australian restarts confirm stable production economics at current prices. For junior lithium developers, the price softness reflects cyclical supply recovery rather than structural demand weakness — EV battery orders and stationary energy storage demand data remain robust — and the market is likely to tighten again when Bald Hill and Finniss inventories are absorbed into active offtake.

headline: ANTIMONY: $4.5B BY 2036, BUT THE CLOCK IS THE PROBLEM — Not Finding It, But Permitting It Fast Enough
snippet: A new market analysis projects the global antimony market will reach $4.5 billion by 2036, but identifies permitting timelines — not geological scarcity — as the binding Western supply chain constraint. China controls approximately 50% of global antimony production and 80-90% of refined output, and has imposed progressive export controls since 2023. The US, EU and Canada have each classified antimony as a critical defence material — essential in armour-piercing ammunition, military electronics, flame retardants and semiconductor alloys — creating government demand that competes directly with industrial uses. The analysis argues that known non-Chinese deposits are sufficient to meet projected demand, but the standard 10-15 year permitting window in most Western jurisdictions means projects entering review today cannot address the 2026-2030 demand surge. Projects with accelerated permitting pathways — particularly those in New Zealand (Fast-Track Approvals) and Australia (NSW accelerated mining processes) — command premium multiples precisely because they can reach production inside the structural supply gap window rather than arriving after it has already closed.
